A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UnSeenTimeQA and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on six existing TSQA benchmarks and UnSeenTimeQA, including model accuracy, depth analyses, and manually classified reasoning errors.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original few-shot evaluations in Appendix B, Tables 5–6, and Figures 7–10.

M1.justification: The planning-based benchmark construction, event-tracking dictionary, question generation, and answer rules remain unchanged. Few-shot prompting is an additional evaluation condition, not a revision to the proposed benchmark-generation method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six existing benchmarks and the same English logistics benchmark with 10,800 samples, four difficulty levels, and three question types. Few-shot experiments retain this coverage. Appendix templates and all twelve worked examples are unchanged after renumbering.

E2.justification: The evaluated model roster remains Gemma-2-9B/27B, Llama-3.1-8B/70B, and GPT-4o. Section 3 retains its GPT-4 comparisons and context conditions. Appendix B changes prompting settings for the existing models without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: v3 adds a complete two-shot chain-of-thought evaluation alongside v2's zero-shot experiments, covering all five models and all benchmark categories. Prompts contain two randomly selected benchmark examples excluded from test samples. The original accuracy metric, test-split sizes, and zero-shot protocol remain.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a systematic sensitivity analysis testing whether demonstrations alleviate the failures observed with zero-shot prompting. Tables 5–6 and Figures 7–10 compare prompting conditions across models, difficulties, and question types. The existing depth plots and reasoning-error analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means and standard deviations across three data splits; the few-shot tables follow that practice. Changed standard-deviation values are result updates. Appendix A's newly described three sampling rounds construct existing 150-question subsets rather than introduce repeated model runs or new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds the full few-shot result matrix and average columns. Table 6 reports GPT-4o's few-shot hard-parallel average as 46.23%. In retained zero-shot results, GPT-4o hard-serial relative-time accuracy changes from 42.44% to 47.44%; its hypothetical-time standard deviation changes from 5.01 to 3.01. Gemma-2-9B easy relative-time standard deviation changes from 0.00 to 1.22.

T1.justification: The depth definition in Section 4.5 and event semantics are retained. Expanded explanations of depth and concurrency do not introduce new mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the earlier broad statement of inferior synthetic-task performance by explicitly acknowledging good performance on simpler subsets. The principal contributions—synthetic contamination-resistant evaluation, parallel-event reasoning, and identifying LLM weaknesses—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges assuming knowledge cutoff is the primary difference between the compared GPT-4 versions. Section 6 refines the explanation of depth's limitations under parallel execution and suggests alternative complexity metrics. Appendix B interprets demonstration effects, and the former zero-shot-only limitation is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents three 50-question sampling rounds, reviewer assignments, citation recording, and second-reviewer cross-checking. Section 7 specifies random error sampling and manual classification; Appendix B describes demonstration selection and test exclusion. These disclosures expand reproducibility information, while model endpoints, hardware details, templates, and the existing prompt remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Fatemi et al. (2024), Suzgun et al. (2023), and Yao et al. (2024), supporting temporal-reasoning motivation and few-shot evaluation. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites and copyedits across the abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, and limitations. Appendix A gains three subsections, a new Appendix B is inserted, and subsequent appendices are renumbered. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds two few-shot result tables and four multi-panel comparison figures. Tables 2–3 gain average columns and revised spacing. Figure 6 and existing appendix displays relocate, with additional caption edits and pagination changes; their relocation does not represent new scientific content.

improvement.justification: The few-shot study addresses v2's acknowledged lack of demonstration-based testing, while expanded review procedures and a more qualified abstract improve transparency and precision. These gains are tempered by new numerical inconsistencies: Table 5 reports Llama-3.1-70B's easy average as 94.92%, although its displayed component scores average 95.52%. The added evidence remains useful, but the reporting issues limit the overall improvement.
